proof:
Source: the double application of the locality lemma in steps 3 and 5 of the parent proof. Notation: μ := μHE[n], M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient.

1. M is locally finite in U. M is Borel and M ⊆ U (fields measurableSet_carrier, carrier_subset). For compact K ⊆ U, θ ≥ 1 on M (θ is ℕ-valued and positive on M by mult_pos), so μ(M ∩ K) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} 1 dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dμ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult.

2. Apply the sibling lemma tangent_locality with open set U, small set B and large set M: B ⊆ M ⊆ U are Borel and M is locally finite in U by step 1. Hence for μ⌞B-a.e. x, for every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q.

3. Apply tangent_locality with open set U, small set B and large set C, using the hypotheses on B and C. Hence for μ⌞B-a.e. x, for every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q.

4. The field orients of R says: for μ⌞M-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. Since B ⊆ M we have μ⌞B ≤ μ⌞M, so this also holds for μ⌞B-a.e. x.

5. Let x lie outside the union of the three μ⌞B-null exceptional sets of steps 2–4. Take Q from step 4. By step 2 (⟹), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q; by step 3 (⟸), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q; and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. This proves the claim for μ⌞B-a.e. x. ∎
key_steps: The carrier M of an IMRep is Borel and locally Hⁿ-finite in U because θ ≥ 1 on M.
tangent_locality for B ⊆ M and for B ⊆ C: a.e. on B, T_xB = T_xM and T_xB = T_xC.
The orients field of R holds a.e. on B ⊆ M; combine to get T_xC = T_xM oriented by ξ(x).
